Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStreamTest.testBase64EmptyInputStream() feeds an empty input (new byte[0]) and expects an empty output, even when a line length (76) and line separator (CRLF) are specified.
- Issue report: “Base64.encode(new byte[0]) doesn’t return an empty byte array back! It returns CRLF.” This matches the test’s observed behavior.

Code analysis:
- Base64InputStream when constructed with encoding and a line length/line separator uses a Base64 encoder configured with those values: Base64InputStream(InputStream, boolean, int, byte[]) sets this.base64 = new Base64(lineLength, lineSeparator).
- The core encoding logic is in Base64.encode(byte[], int, int). On EOF (inAvail < 0), it executes:
  - Sets eof = true.
  - Emits any pending partial quartet based on modulus (cases 1 and 2).
  - Then unconditionally appends the line separator if lineLength > 0:
    if (lineLength > 0) {
        System.arraycopy(lineSeparator, 0, buf, pos, lineSeparator.length);
        pos += lineSeparator.length;
    }
- For an empty input stream, no data is ever processed, so modulus remains 0 and no Base64 characters are written. However, because lineLength > 0, the code still appends the line separator on EOF. This produces a CRLF output for empty input, violating the expectation of an empty result.

Why the array-based encode(byte[]) doesn’t show this:
- Base64.encode(byte[]) delegates to encodeBase64(byte[], false, isUrlSafe()), which early-returns the input array when binaryData.length == 0, so it correctly yields an empty array and avoids the EOF path above. The bug manifests in streaming usage (e.g., Base64InputStream) or any code path that drives Base64.encode(..., inAvail = -1) with a positive lineLength.

Conclusion:
- The root cause is in Base64.encode(byte[], int, int): on EOF it appends the line separator whenever lineLength > 0, even if no Base64 data was written (modulus == 0 / currentLinePos == 0). The line separator should only be appended if there has been output on the current line. This erroneous unconditional append explains the CRLF output for empty input and the failing test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
